subject: environmental-science
title: Indicators, Keystones and Red Lists
welcome_lead: Some species speak for ecosystems — listen to lichens, otters and frogs.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on indicator species, keystones and IUCN Red List categories.
final_note: A single sentinel species can reveal the health of an entire biome.

concepts.def: Organism whose presence signals environmental quality (e.g., lichens, mayfly nymphs).
Species whose impact on community structure exceeds its abundance (Paine 1969).
Global threat assessment with categories EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD, NE.
Restriction of a species to a defined geographic region.
Species whose conservation indirectly protects many others sharing its habitat.
Charismatic species used to drive conservation campaigns (e.g., giant panda).

walkthroughs.body_html: Mayfly nymphs vanish when BOD rises; lichen species shift along SO₂ gradients. Indicators translate stress into observable change.
Paine's Pisaster removal showed sea stars maintained intertidal diversity. Yellowstone wolves trigger trophic cascades reshaping rivers.
The IUCN uses quantitative criteria on population size, range and decline rate. CR species face ≥80% decline over 10 years or three generations.
